SMTO-HTTP-0023 — SMTO can't reach your saved web service connections

GUID: 5adb8ce5-cb29-4b5e-b652-9d15ce2ab666
Slug: http-profile-unavailable
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • This task needs a saved web service connection, but Parameter Store, where SMTO keeps those connections, is turned off or not available right now. Nothing was sent to the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the app menu and check that it loads and lists your saved connections. If it loads normally, the problem was temporary and SMTO can try the connection again.
  2. If Parameter Store doesn't load or says it is turned off, ask the person who manages SMTO to turn Parameter Store back on for the server and restart it. Parameter Store can be switched off in the server's setup, and only someone with access to the server can change that.
  3. Once Parameter Store works, ask SMTO in the conversation to connect to the service again using the connection's exact name. SMTO reads the saved connection fresh when it connects, so it picks up the restored store.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store lists your connections and SMTO connects to the service without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or saved connections to try to fix this; they hold your saved settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An HTTP operation that needs a saved profile could not run because Parameter Store is absent from the execution context or disabled in the accepted configuration.

What this means

  • Parameter Store is absent or disabled in the accepted configuration for an operation that needs a saved profile. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Parameter Store is absent or disabled in the accepted configuration for an operation that needs a saved profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether the run has a Parameter Store and whether its accepted feature setting enables it.

How to fix it

  • http.connect, http.request, http.inspect_connections and http.manage_connection raise this when _parameter_store_from_context returns no store or config.agent_parameter_store_enabled is false. Set AOR_AGENT_PARAMETER_STORE_ENABLED=true (the default), confirm the Parameter Store database is reachable, restart the Server, then reselect the exact profile.
  • Restore Parameter Store access and reselect the intended current profile.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended current run can read the exact saved profile through the supported store.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
